children: Federal Reserve Bank of New York President John Williams said on Thursday rate increases likely lie ahead for the central bank as it seeks to get high levels of inflation back to 2%.

“The economy is strong, labor market continues to strengthen, and inflation is persistent,” Williams said at an event in New York. “We'll need to take actions over time that will ensure that we get inflation back to our 2% goal in a timely manner and on a sustained basis,” he said, adding, “We still have work to do…to get monetary policy to the right place.”

title: Fed's Williams says central bank has 'work to do' to get inflation back on target
